clue.text: ABC is primarily suitable, perhaps, for these?

definitions.text: ABC is primarily suitable, perhaps, for these?

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the preceding letters might be arranged some other way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: primarily means at the start, so only the opening letter of the next word counts

parts.note: first letter of suitable

explanation.surface: Someone wonders which audience an alphabet primer would suit.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the ABC is the most elementary material there is, so it suits the BASICS.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning one's ABC is the proverbial image of mastering fundamentals, the elementary groundwork of any subject.

clue.text: Maybe Holly's husband stuck behind large vehicle

indicators.note: stuck behind places one element after the other in sequence

parts.note: a bus is a large passenger vehicle
H is the standard abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A woman named Holly's husband is trapped behind a lorry in traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: Holly looks like a woman's name with a husband, but it is the plant, and 's is short for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Holly is an evergreen shrub, so it is an example of a bush, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Louder individual welcomed among rabble

indicators.note: something welcomed among a group is taken inside it

parts.note: shower is British slang for a contemptible bunch of people
I as the Roman numeral one, a single individual

explanation.surface: A loud person is let into the midst of an unruly crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a 'shower' is a useless or disreputable group, as in 'what a shower!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Louder in the sense of more garish or flashy, as of clothing, is a synonym for more ostentatious.

clue.text: Two lots of Greek letters containing a rhetorical device

indicators.note: containing means the first group holds the next item inside it

parts.note: first lot: the Greek letter chi, plural
taken as written
second lot: the Greek letter mu, plural

explanation.surface: A grammar note says a figure of speech involves two sets of Greek symbols.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two lots' supplies two separate plural letters, and the A sits inside the first. Fittingly, the device is named after chi, X, for its crossed shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Chiasmus is the rhetorical figure where terms are repeated in reverse order, as in 'fair is foul and foul is fair'.

clue.text: Sewage initially disappearing after a flush

indicators.note: initially disappearing tells us the opening letter goes missing
after puts the shortened word behind the next item

parts.note: taken as written
effluent is liquid waste or sewage

explanation.surface: Waste water vanishes once someone pulls the toilet chain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flush' reads as the toilet, but it is the adjective meaning well off with money.
explanation.definitionFit: Being flush means having plenty of money, so it is a synonym for wealthy or rich.

clue.text: Spat on celebs one caught promoting social inequality

parts.note: a spat is a quarrel
the A-list is the top tier of celebrities
Roman numeral one
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone spits on celebrities caught pushing an unequal society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spat' looks like the past tense of spit, but it is the noun for a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Feudalism was a rigid hierarchy of lords and serfs, so a feudalistic outlook upholds entrenched class inequality.

clue.text: Communicate false info about mafiosi, periodically

indicators.note: about means going round, so the false info wraps the other letters

parts.note: a lie is false information

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of mafiosi

explanation.surface: An informant spreads disinformation about the Mafia from time to time.
explanation.definitionFit: To liaise is to keep in contact and cooperate with another party, so it means to communicate.

clue.text: Volte-face from old chap in Parisian street entrance

indicators.note: a volte-face is a complete about-turn, so the whole construction faces the other way
in places one item inside the street word

parts.note: rue is French for street
O is the abbreviation for old
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: An elderly man does an about-turn at the doorway of a Paris street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' looks like a noun for a doorway, but it is the verb, stressed on the second syllable, meaning to delight.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to captivate them, and enamour likewise means to fill with love or delight.

clue.text: Online commenter's weight has someone laughing about it

indicators.note: about it means surrounding the item just named, the weight

parts.note: one who titters, laughing nervously
W is the physics symbol for weight

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at an internet poster's body weight.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's means 'has', and W goes in after the first T.
explanation.definitionFit: A twitterer posts short messages on Twitter, a social media platform, so is one who comments online.

clue.text: See 22 Down
Corrupt Raja in middle India gets the lingo there?

indicators.note: corrupt means twisted out of its proper state, so the letters are jumbled
in places the jumbled ruler inside the word for the middle

parts.note: the gut is the belly, one's middle
an Indian ruler's title, letters rearranged
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A crooked maharaja in central India picks up the local tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 'India' from the wordplay: 'there' is India, and the question mark admits it is only one of its languages.
explanation.definitionFit: Gujarati is a language spoken in the western Indian state of Gujarat, so it is one lingo of India.

clue.text: Students getting job after good result of degree in letters

indicators.note: after puts the first two items behind the last one named

parts.note: a first is the top class of British university degree
a class is a group of students
a post is a job

explanation.surface: Students land jobs after earning top honours in a literature degree.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'first' is the highest grade of British honours degree. 'Letters' reads as the academic subject, but means things sent by mail.
explanation.definitionFit: First-class post is the faster, dearer Royal Mail service for letters in Britain, so letters are sent by it.

clue.text: Silly mesh hot pants for a consumer of garments

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are a mess to be reworked

parts.note: a clot is a silly person
these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sneers that hot mesh underwear is a silly choice of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like trousers or underwear, fitting the clothing surface, but is slang for rubbish. 'Silly' stands as a noun, as in 'you silly'.
explanation.definitionFit: The larvae of the clothes moth eat wool and fabric, so the insect literally consumes garments.

clue.text: Playing our piano, starts to compose concerto for horn

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are performed in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: starts to means taking the opening letters of the following words

parts.note: first letters of compose and concerto

explanation.surface: Musicians at a piano begin writing a horn concerto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horn' looks like the brass instrument in this musical scene, but it is the horn of plenty.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornucopia is Latin for 'horn of plenty', the overflowing goat's horn symbolising abundance.

clue.text: Dealing with colour, check an artist like Turner eschews navy

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check

indicators.note: eschews means avoids, so a letter is left out of the word

parts.note: J M W Turner was a Romantic painter
N is the abbreviation for navy

explanation.surface: An art critic studies colour and observes that Turner avoided navy blue in his palette.
explanation.walkthrough: Navy looks like the shade of blue in this colour scene, but it gives only N, removed from ROMANTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Chromatic comes from Greek chroma, colour, and describes anything relating to or produced by colour.

clue.text: Beer drained by Republicans — it's bitter!

indicators.note: drained means emptied, so only the outer shell of the word remains

parts.note: first and last letters of beer
R for Republican, doubled for the plural
joins the two pieces

explanation.surface: A drinker finishes a pint of bitter as Republicans look on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bitter' looks like the British beer, which fits the drinking scene, but here it means bitterly cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Brrr is the exclamation people make when shivering, said when the weather is bitterly cold.

clue.text: Around hostelry, suppose this may get drunk

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the verb wraps round the hostelry

parts.note: to guess is to suppose
an inn is a hostelry

explanation.surface: Around the pub, one supposes someone may end up drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get drunk' looks like a person becoming intoxicated, but is passive: this is something that gets drunk, a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Guinness is a famous Irish stout, a beer consumed in pubs, so it is a thing that is drunk.

clue.text: Bank official rings Head of Eurobank

indicators.note: rings means encircles, so the official surrounds the next letter

parts.note: ref is short for referee, a sports official

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the following word

parts.note: first letter of Eurobank

explanation.surface: A banking official telephones the boss of a European bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks like a financial institution, but is the sandbank sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A reef is a ridge of rock, sand or coral near the water's surface, a kind of underwater bank.

clue.text: Alluring person's frenetic, topless dancing

indicators.note: topless means without its top, so the first letter is removed
dancing letters move about into a new arrangement

parts.note: frenetic without its first letter

explanation.surface: A seductive person is frantic about topless dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice is to lure or tempt, so an enticer is someone who allures others.

clue.text: Society dance which includes tango, say, for one throwing a ball

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for society

indicators.note: which includes means the dance holds the next letter within it

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance
T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: A society dance features a tango, a fitting number for whoever is throwing a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throwing a ball' suggests hosting a dance, matching the society scene, but means hurling a heavy metal ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot putter is an athlete who hurls the shot, a heavy metal ball, for distance in field events.

clue.text: War god placed towards the top part of Roman decoration

indicators.note: in a down clue, moving towards the top means reading upwards

parts.note: Ares is the Greek god of war
set means placed

explanation.surface: A statue of the god of war is set near the top of a Roman ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is one of the small tiles used in Roman mosaics, so it is a component of that decoration.

clue.text: Little growth in Shanghai as no business is on the up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the letters from bottom to top
in says the letters sit inside the following words

parts.note: letters running across Shanghai, as, no and business

explanation.surface: A modest economic upturn in Shanghai while firms are on the rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little growth' reads as weak economic figures, but means a miniature plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonsai is a tree kept deliberately dwarfed in a pot, literally a small growing thing.

clue.text: In Minsk etc., so-so tours a problem for traveller

indicators.note: tours suggests the letters wander about and end up in a new order

parts.note: every letter of these words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A mediocre tour of Minsk and similar cities causes a traveller trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Motion sickness is nausea caused by moving vehicles, a common affliction of people on journeys.

clue.text: Not a single firm invested in huge capital returns in the Halifax region

parts.note: no means not a single one

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it

parts.note: vast means huge
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: returns means comes back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, as does capital, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: No company has put money into the great capital, which is losing value around Halifax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money or a city, but is the old adjective for excellent; A1 means the same. 'Halifax' is the Canadian city, not the Yorkshire town or the British bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Halifax is the capital of the Canadian province Nova Scotia, so the province is the region around that city.

clue.text: Corpulent friar's bound for confectionery store

parts.note: Friar Tuck, the stout monk of the Robin Hood legend
a bound is a leap or hop

explanation.surface: A fat friar is heading off to buy sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound for' looks like heading towards, but 'bound' is the jump and 'for' links. A tuck shop is a British school's snack and sweet shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuck shop sells sweets and snacks, tuck being British slang for food, so it is a confectionery store.

clue.text: Three bananas, round or straight?

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the number goes wild and rearranges

parts.note: these letters rearranged
O has a round shape

explanation.surface: A shopper asks whether to buy three curved bananas or straight ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like fruit in a shape question, but is slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Hetero, short for heterosexual, and straight are both informal words for attracted to the opposite sex.

clue.text: My hotel in Med resort in coastal route

parts.note: cor! is a British exclamation of surprise, like my!

indicators.note: in places the hotel letter inside the resort name

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Mediterranean coast
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone's hotel stands in a Mediterranean resort on the coast road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks like a possessive, but is the exclamation 'my!'; cor is its British slang equivalent.
explanation.definitionFit: A corniche is a road cut along a cliff face, especially the famous coast roads of the Riviera.

clue.text: European country's sea unfortunately full of trash

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters fall out of order
full of means the scrambled word holds the next item inside

parts.note: these letters rearranged
to trash and to pan both mean to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: A European nation's coastal waters are sadly polluted with rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trash' looks like rubbish floating in the sea, but is the verb for slating a show.
explanation.definitionFit: España is the Spanish name for Spain, a country of Europe.
